title: Open extension preserves bounded-target internal-Hom continuity
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use the ordinary uncompleted category $D(B_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $v:V\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with $T$ topologically Noetherian (descending chains of closed subsets stabilize). All sites and indexing categories are small in the fixed module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Filtered colimits below are termwise sheaf colimits of functorial complex representatives, and all comparison maps are induced by the original cocone. For $A\in D(B_T)$ say $P_T(A)$ if (i) for every small filtered diagram $(N_i)$ of complexes with a common cohomological lower bound $c$, the evaluation-induced map $\varinjlim_i R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(A,N_i)\to R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(A,\varinjlim_iN_i)$ is an isomorphism, and (ii) there is an integer $d_A$, independent of $N,c$, such that $R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(A,N)\in D^{\ge c+d_A}$ whenever $N\in D^{\ge c}$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. If $P_V(A)$ holds with a chosen bound $d_A$, then $P_T(v_!A)$ holds with the same bound, where $v_!$ is exact module extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. The comparison for $v_!A$ is the evaluation-induced comparison; no constructibility assumption on $A$ is required.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(2) and Lemma 6.8.12: agent internal-sheaf, filtered-colimit refinement of open-extension stability.

proof.text: For each affine open $W\subset T$, the inverse image $V\times_TW$ identifies with the subset $v(V)\cap W$ of $T$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], so $v$ is quasi-compact. An open immersion is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](a), hence quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus $v$ satisfies the qcqs hypothesis used below. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme] to $T\setminus v(V)$ to choose a complementary closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$. This choice is only to instantiate the existing open/closed Hom formula; the open formula and its comparison map do not depend on $i$.

source.place: Tag 04ZA, lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact; schemes.tex Tags 01L7, 01K7 and 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme

proof.text: For $S=T,V$, the sheaf category $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathrm{Ab})$ is Grothendieck by [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck]. Its closed additive tensor structure is [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Therefore [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] applies to $B_S$ and makes $\operatorname{Mod}_{B_S}$ Grothendieck. In particular its filtered colimits are exact, by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. By [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits], $H^q(\varinjlim C_i)=\varinjlim H^q(C_i)$ for the termwise colimits in this proof. Consequently these colimits preserve a common cohomological lower bound and take objectwise quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus the good truncations and functorial representatives in the cited pushforward continuity statement compute precisely the colimits specified in the item.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, proof of (1): filtered colimits are t-exact; the strict-complex interpretation uses the cited exact-colimit homology theorem

proof.text: By [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], the coefficient-compatible $v^*$ on module objects is exact. It is a left adjoint by [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], so [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] identifies $\varinjlim_i v^*N_i$ with $v^*(\varinjlim_iN_i)$ by the map induced by the original cocone. Exactness gives $H^q(v^*N)=v^*H^q(N)$, so it preserves $D^{\ge c}$ and all quasi-isomorphisms. Its termwise derived functor is therefore the same $v^*$ on the ordinary categories under consideration.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, proof of (2), open-immersion case: inverse image is t-exact and commutes with colimits

proof.text: For later use, $Rv_*$ preserves every lower bound $b$. Indeed the Grothendieck source category has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. If $M\in D(B_V)^{\ge b}$, choose a complex representing it which is zero below $b$, using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. The resolution of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono] gives a quasi-isomorphism to an injective complex $I^\bullet$ still zero below $b$. This complex is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Hence $Rv_*M$ is represented by the termwise complex $v_*I^\bullet$, by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Since an additive functor takes zero to zero, this complex is zero below $b$, proving $Rv_*M\in D(B_T)^{\ge b}$. No upper cohomological-dimension bound is used.

source.place: Tags 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist (3), and 070J, lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective; total right derived pushforward as in the cited definition

proof.text: With the complementary $i$ from step 1, the open clause of [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas] supplies the natural isomorphism $\theta_N:R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(v_!A,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv_*R\mathcal Hom_{B_V}(A,v^*N)$. Its statement applies to arbitrary $A,N$ in the ordinary uncompleted categories, not just constructible objects, and specifies evaluation/adjunction compatibility. The coefficient ring in this formula is $B_S=p_S^*\Lambda$, for $S=T,V$. The pushforward in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] is the ordinary uncompleted one for $\Lambda_S=p_S^*\Lambda$, on sectionwise module sheaves. The section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies these with the internal $B_S$-modules used here; it is the identity on underlying sheaves and restriction maps, so it is exact, keeps K-injectives and commutes with $v_*$ and termwise colimits. Hence both $Rv_*$ agree.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, proof of (2): internal Hom adjunction for an immersion and the open-immersion case; the normalized formula is the cited existing node

proof.text: If $N\in D(B_T)^{\ge c}$, then $v^*N\in D(B_V)^{\ge c}$ by step 3. Hypothesis $P_V(A)$(ii) gives $R\mathcal Hom_{B_V}(A,v^*N)\in D(B_V)^{\ge c+d_A}$. Apply step 4 with $b=c+d_A$ and then $\theta_N$ from step 5. This proves $R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(v_!A,N)\in D(B_T)^{\ge c+d_A}$, with the original $d_A$, independently of $N$ and $c$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, proof of (2), lower-bound check for the internal-Hom factors

proof.text: Let $(N_i)$ have common lower bound $c$, and set $F_i=R\mathcal Hom_{B_V}(A,v^*N_i)$. They share the bound $c+d_A$ by $P_V(A)$(ii) and step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] to $v$ and $(F_i)$, using step 1 for qcqs and step 2 for its functorial-complex interpretation. This gives the canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_i Rv_*F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv_*(\varinjlim_iF_i)$. Hypothesis $P_V(A)$(i), applied to $(v^*N_i)$, and the original-cocone identification of step 3 give $\varinjlim_iF_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{B_V}(A,v^*\varinjlim_iN_i)$. Applying $Rv_*$ and conjugating by $\theta$ from step 5 proves an isomorphism between the two sides of $P_T(v_!A)$(i).

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1) and proof of (2), open case; apply bounded-target pushforward continuity to the uniformly bounded internal-Hom diagram

proof.text: Write $\iota_i:N_i\to N=\varinjlim_iN_i$ for the original cocone. The first map in step 7 has components $Rv_*(F_i\to\varinjlim_kF_k)$. By the definition of the comparison in $P_V(A)$(i), the second map carries this component to $Rv_*R\mathcal Hom_{B_V}(A,v^*\iota_i)$. Naturality of $\theta$ in [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas] says exactly that this component, conjugated by $\theta_{N_i}$ and $\theta_N^{-1}$, is $R\mathcal Hom_{B_T}(v_!A,\iota_i)$. The colimit universal property therefore identifies the resulting map with the evaluation-induced comparison specified in the item. Together with step 6 this proves both clauses of $P_T(v_!A)$ with the same bound.

split_report.summary: Proved conditional open-extension stability using existing evaluation-normalized internal-Hom identities and bounded-below qcqs pushforward continuity. Checked topological Noetherianity suffices for qcqs, exact restriction and exact filtered colimits, and proved preservation of the identical lower bound with a supported injective resolution. Identified the resulting comparison on every original cocone component. No new nodes, no statement change.

Uses the open case of Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Lemma 5.3; the unit route and chapter are unchanged.
